title: Impulse
examples: How is impulse related to the force applied?
Can you give an example of impulse in everyday life?
What does a large impulse mean for an object?

explain.say: Today we are learning about impulse in physics.

items: Impulse is the change in momentum.
It is calculated by force times time.

explain.say: Impulse is equal to the change in momentum.
The change in momentum means final minus initial momentum.
A large force applied over a short time gives large impulse.

draw.text: Large F over short t = Large Impulse

explain.say: Crumple zones are designed to increase the time of impact.
Airbags work by increasing the time over which the force acts.

faq.a: Airbags increase the time duration of the collision impact. According to the impulse equation, increasing time reduces the average force.
asks: How does time affect the force in a crash?
Does a bigger airbag mean less force?

faq.q: What is momentum, and how is it calculated?
faq.a: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and its velocity. You calculate it by multiplying mass by velocity.

faq.q: Is impulse the same as momentum?
faq.a: No, impulse is the change in momentum. It measures the effect of force over a period of time.
asks: Is impulse the same as force?
What is the difference between impulse and momentum?

faq.q: What happens if the time of impact is very short?
faq.a: If the time of impact is very short, the force exerted on the body will be very large. This can cause serious injury.
asks: What is the danger of a sudden stop?
How does short time relate to force?

faq.q: Do crumple zones work by changing momentum?
faq.a: Crumple zones manage the collision by extending the time over which the vehicle decelerates. This reduces the average force experienced by the occupants.
asks: Are crumple zones about force or time?
How do cars absorb impact energy?

facts: Impulse is mathematically defined as the change in momentum.
The formula relating these concepts is Impulse equals mass times the change in velocity.
Safety features like airbags increase the time interval of impact.
A larger time interval results in a smaller average force for the same momentum change.

quiz.say: A car hits a wall. If the car's speed is high, what will happen to the force experienced by the passengers?

options.show: The force depends on the car's color.
options.say: The force depends on the car's color.

options.show: The force will be very large.
options.say: The force will be very large.

quiz.why: High speed means a large change in momentum, which requires a large force over a short time.

wrong.0: This is wrong because stopping from speed always involves a significant force.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the physics only depends on mass and velocity changes.
wrong.3: This is wrong because momentum change is directly related to the force applied.

quiz.say: Which safety feature is designed to increase the time of impact?
quiz.why: Crumple zones work by deforming slowly, which extends the time over which the car stops, thus lowering the force.

wrong.0: Seatbelts primarily restrain the body, not necessarily increasing the time of the whole impact.
wrong.1: While airbags also increase time, crumple zones are the primary structure designed for this overall purpose.
wrong.2: Tires help with friction but do not control the overall duration of the major collision impact.

quiz.say: If the change in momentum ($\Delta p$) is constant, how must the force ($\text{F}$) and time ($\Delta t$) relate?

options.show: Force must be independent of time.
options.say: Force must be independent of time.

options.show: Force must be proportional to the square of time.
options.say: Force must be proportional to the square of time.

options.show: Force must be inversely proportional to time.
options.say: Force must be inversely proportional to time.

options.show: Force must be directly proportional to time.
options.say: Force must be directly proportional to time.

quiz.why: Since F equals $\Delta p$ divided by $\Delta t$, if $\Delta t$ increases, F must decrease to keep $\Delta p$ the same.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the relationship $\text{F} = \Delta p / \Delta t$ clearly shows dependence.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the relationship is linear, not quadratic.
wrong.3: This is wrong because if force increased with time, the impulse would become much larger than needed.
